title: Divine testimony and revelation — object of faith’s certainty
source_text: XVI. Sed praeter illa supra enumerata, quae mentem movere & impellere possunt ut firmiter & certo rei assentiatur, unum superest, nempe, testimonium divinum, & divina revelatio; quae objectum est fidei illius de cujus certitudine disputatio praesens instituta est. Porro illam esse summam & absolutam, & ipsam scientiarum certitudinem superare, non tantum agnoscit scholarum consensus, sed communis quoque Christianorum sensus: ita ut etiam in sermone triviali, articuli fidei pro exemplo rei, omnium certissimae, nominari soleant.
pass_a_gloss: But besides those things enumerated above which can move and drive the mind to assent firmly and certainly to a thing, one remains: namely, divine testimony and divine revelation — which is the object of that faith concerning whose certainty the present disputation is instituted. Further, that it is the highest and absolute, and surpasses even the certainty of the sciences, not only the consensus of the schools acknowledges, but also the common sense of Christians: so that even in everyday speech the articles of faith are wont to be named as the example of a thing most certain of all.
pass_b_english: Beyond listed movers: divine testimony / revelation.
Object of the faith whose certainty this tract disputes.
Schools + common Christian sense: highest, absolute — above scientiae; everyday ‘articles of faith’ as most-certain example.
